Non-metallic & insulating components
Plastic insulators, wear parts and housings

Insulating plates, wear components and machined blocks place different demands on a polymer. Specify the grade for the operating environment and loads, then review the machining and measurement conditions.

Geometry & process
For insulating components, wear parts, seals and lightweight structural pieces. Milling and turning cover drilled blocks, gears, rollers, thin walls, deep pockets and multi-axis holes.
Size & workholding
Send a 3D model with the overall dimensions and stock size. Low-stress workholding and temperature control address deformation. Review clamping space, tool access, thin sections and assembly loads together.
Material & finish
PEEK, PTFE, polyimide, nylon, acetal/Delrin, HDPE, UHMW, acrylic and polycarbonate are listed in the plastic machining service. Specify the exact polymer grade, fillers and stock condition. Define edge quality, cleaning and mating-surface requirements.
Grades to discuss

Engineering plastics: POM (acetal) · PTFE · PEEK · Nylon · PA6 · PA66 · ABS · PC · PVC · PP

Specify the polymer grade and condition. Acetal and Delrin are not treated as different base polymers here; confirm a branded grade if required.

Select play to view the original footage.
Drawing & acceptance
Drawing requirements

Give the exact polymer grade, fillers and stock condition. Identify temperature, moisture, chemical exposure and electrical requirements relevant to selection.

Mark thin walls and deep pockets, along with press fits and inserts. Include assembly loads and any permitted geometry changes.

Inspection and acceptance

Agree measurement and conditioning requirements where material behavior affects acceptance. Define hole position, flatness and mating-surface criteria.

Specify edge, cleanliness and surface requirements; a product photograph is not evidence of electrical, food-contact or medical compliance.

Agree the measurement method and required records before production.
